launches.title: Supernova 🌌 Create, document and distribute your next design system
launches.tagline: Supernova helps to create, maintain, scale and adopt design systems on any scale
launches.body:
**Building, maintaining and adopting design system is hard. Really hard.**

There are almost no tools to help and data needed to build one are all over the place - in Figma, Storybook, maybe in Notion or Confluence, resulting in a huge mess and teams struggling with adopting your creation. And to make the matter worse, many teams don’t know how to build a proper design system in the first place.

Hey you, thanks for checking our platform [👋](https://emojipedia.org/waving-hand/) It’s Jiri, CEO, and founder of [Supernova.io](http://Supernova.io). Let me take you on a tour!

### How it works

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=64208&key=user_uploads/131850/1136c993-cf2e-4a0a-9a47-fd017f5bed1f)

With Supernova, you can create, manage, document, and distribute a design system at one place. We have thousands of teams onboard who are in many cases seeing multiples in terms of increase in efficiency and the adoption of the design system - plus who doesn’t love a good and fun experience when creating it? Here are some main features you’ll love.

### Design System Management

Design systems consist of components, tokens, assets, fonts, branding resources and many more disparate elements - with Supernova, everything lives together, forming a coherent and easily maintainable design system using power tools at your disposal, such as asset and component manager or a dashboard to manage all design system processes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=64208&key=user_uploads/131850/5bd77bb6-4bc3-4582-b9aa-6086d5e5a561)

### Documentation

We got carried away (a lot) and basically created a replica of Notion editor (amazing editing experience!) focused on documenting design systems. You can document and also share/distribute every aspect of your design system using all data from your libraries.

Best of all, the editor feels like magic because it keeps your documentation up to date, changing the content automatically as you change and improve your design system. No more changing 500 pages of the documentation manually!

We even made our own user documentation using it - [check it out](https://learn.supernova.io/)!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=64208&key=user_uploads/131850/7072ff7f-ac54-47df-87c9-bbc46111242c)

### Automated synchronization and distribution

We all come from automation backgrounds - and so Supernova is packed with automation from top (importing and synchronizing design and code you create in other tools) to bottom (automated export, synchronization with codebases, automatically rewriting your docs).

As an example, you can setup Supernova in such a way that if you create a new icon in Figma, a pull request will be open against all your repository with that icon, properly formatted. Now imagine if you add 10 icons, for React, iOS, and Android, with 4 different themes and 10 different white-labeled apps - talk about saving time.

### Too much to write here

We poured our heart and soul into making the best design system platform possible and there are hundreds of small things that make design systems a better experience with Supernova - and your life better day-to-day if you are tasked with creating and maintaining it.

If you struggle with your design system, just let us know or try out the platform right away (<https://supernova.io/>), it is free to start with and scales extremely well even for large teams!

Can’t wait to have you onboard, enjoy!

Hi friends! Vikas here from LightTwist, excited to share our new launch!

**Check out our 45 second launch video here**:[ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fYGvhRrOXBI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fYGvhRrOXBI)

**TL;DR:** LightTwist lets you record and stream in a realistic virtual studio, even if your guests and co-hosts are remote.

**The problem**: Your video/podcast/webinar looks like a boring Zoom call. If you want to upgrade to something that looks like a real show you need to build out a physical video studio and bring people into it.

**The solution:** LightTwist is a virtual video studio that runs in Chrome - all the heavy compute is done in the cloud using realtime computer vision, Unreal Engine 5, and WebRTC. This means you can record and stream your show, product announcement, or webinar in a realistic virtual studio, even if your guests and co-hosts are remote.

**We’re launching publicly next week, July 1 at 9 am PT but wanted to give early access to YC!**

**Launch YC special offer 1 (up to 10 spots) - Buy a Show!** Purchase [here](https://buy.stripe.com/9B6aEY7YX0Iv0Bo6Xz5c40b)

**YC special offer 2 - 90% off LightTwist for 2 months!** Sign up [here](https://studio.lighttwist.com/onboarding/9996d28e-75a0-476b-ad7b-621d43200f95) (use promo code **LAUNCHYC2026**)

I started LightTwist in 2021 after seeing how Industrial Light and Magic built a huge 360 surround stage for the Mandalorian show where they had a tracked camera and rendered the scene in realtime using Unreal Engine.

I’ve started a few computer vision companies (RedLaser, a barcode scanning price comparison app -[acquired by eBay](https://www.wsj.com/articles/BL-DGB-15645), [Twindo.com](http://Twindo.com) - FKA Occipital), so I thought there had to be a way to make virtual production much more accessible using computer vision and software engineering.

We’ve gone through several iterations, started as an iOS app for filmmakers, built a macOS app to be an awesome virtual camera for Zoom/etc, but have gotten a lot more traction once we positioned LightTwist as a virtual video studio and rebuilt it to run in the cloud.

We’ve signed an enterprise customer using LightTwist to power their video streaming platform (not yet announced!), and we’ve been iterating with other creators and studios including building a gameshow for Jimmy Fallon’s video production company.

We’re excited to be rolling this out publicly!

launches.tagline: We help infrastructure survey and engineering teams turn raw point cloud data into engineering-ready CAD/GIS deliverables up to 100x faster.
launches.body:
Hi everyone! 

We’re [Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexbaikovitz/), [Zach](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zachsussman/), [Haowen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/haowensh/), and [Michael ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mmong/)- co-founders of [Mach9](https://mach9.ai/). 

**📍TLDR**: 

Mach9's Digital Surveyor 2 is a geospatial platform that turns LiDAR point clouds into engineering-ready deliverables up to 100x faster. Its AI-powered extraction engine identifies and extracts linear features — including curbs, pavement edges, guardrails, and barriers — and learns from each user's edits to improve accuracy over time.

Survey and engineering teams at Langan, Olsson, HDR, Woolpert, Michael Baker International, and major utilities and state DOTs already use it in production.

Check out our Digital Surveyor 2 Launch Video:

[**https://youtu.be/XoISK5nx87E?si=mzcrxg5uI3hynSm2**](https://youtu.be/XoISK5nx87E?si=mzcrxg5uI3hynSm2)

**❌ The Problem**

Every road, bridge, fiber network, and utility corridor project starts with a survey. Increasingly, that survey is done with LiDAR scans encompassing millions of points.

**But here's the thing**: Collecting data isn't the hard part anymore, turning it into engineering ready deliverables is. Today, that work is being done manually. Skilled technicians sit in front of a screen and trace features one by one across potentially thousands of features. Paint lines, curbs, poles, signs, guardrails. Mile after mile.

**As a result**: Firms turn down work they could win, deadlines slip, and the most expensive bottleneck of the workflow is the part that hasn't changed in 20 years.

**✅ Our Solution**

Digital Surveyor 2 is a web-based CAD application where AI works alongside drafters to extract features from point cloud data dramatically faster — without sacrificing the precision their clients require.

Here's what makes it different:

🔹 **AI that drafts with you**. 

The feature extraction engine in Digital Surveyor 2 suggests linear features, such as curbs, pavement edges, guardrails, and barriers directly from LiDAR point clouds — and adapts to the user’s drawing patterns. As users draw, the software picks up on their patterns and refines its suggestions in real time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99241&key=user_uploads/311199/ca66f2e8-267b-4693-83ec-81b92eabb558)

🔹 **Field-to-finish in one environment**. 

Ingest point cloud data from any system such as RIEGL, Trimble, or Leica scanners. Extract features with AI-assisted workflows and precision tools. Easily QA everything in 3D. Export directly into AutoCAD, MicroStation, or ESRI. No switching between tools. No preprocessing pipeline.

🔹 **Built for the people who do this work**. 

DS2 was designed so that a surveyor who knows where points go in the field can be productive on day one. Surveyors, field techs, and project managers can easily be working in it with minimal ramp time or CAD expertise.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99241&key=user_uploads/311199/e5e82676-f1fd-4bcd-bd86-fcca46636e29)

We're especially looking to connect with survey and engineering leaders, mobile mapping teams, CAD/GIS technicians, and geospatial production leads.
* **🚀 Try it yourself** — If your team is turning point clouds into deliverables today, we'd love to show you what DS2 can do. [Get started here](http://mach9.ai/get-started?utm_source=YC&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=launch_post).
* 💼 **We're hiring** — We're building engineering software to transform the $3 trillion global infrastructure industry. If you want to work on hard problems at the intersection of AI, geospatial, and computer graphics, we're scaling across GTM, engineering, and operations. Check out our open roles [here](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mach9).

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re launching Unlayer Elements, an open-source React content layer that lets developers and AI agents create emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same codebase. Write once in React, render everywhere.

Today, we’re launching something new and open source:

# Unlayer Elements

An open-source React content layer for developers and AI agents to create emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same codebase.

GitHub: <https://github.com/unlayer/elements>\
Docs: <https://docs.unlayer.com/elements>\
Demo: <https://youtu.be/-ZoMlPYUbtk>

## **The Problem**

Every SaaS product eventually needs content creation.

At first, it’s just one transactional email.

Then it becomes welcome emails, password resets, receipts, invoices, reports, landing pages, PDFs, internal templates, previews, exports, and visual editing.

Most teams end up maintaining separate systems for each output:

* one system for email templates
* one system for web pages
* one system for PDFs
* one system for visual editing
* one system for exports

The content is often similar, but the implementation is different.

This becomes even more important now that AI agents are generating more code and content. Agents can create fast, but teams still need the output to be structured, reusable, version-controlled, and production-ready.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105004&key=user_uploads/105300/5911c2cd-ca33-48e8-86ff-72e1ce4fcfe7)

## **What We Built**

We built Unlayer Elements: open-source React components for creating emails, web pages, and PDFs from the same codebase.

Developers can use familiar components like:

* <Email>
* <Page>
* <Document>
* <Row>
* <Column>
* <Heading>
* <Paragraph>
* <Button>
* <Image>
* <Custom>

Each output mode is tuned for where the content will live:

* <Email> renders email-safe table HTML
* <Page> renders responsive web HTML
* <Document> renders print-ready HTML for PDFs and documents

Same component system. Different surfaces.

A few examples of what you can build:

* Transactional emails
* Landing pages
* Web versions of emails
* Invoices
* Receipts
* Reports
* Internal template galleries
* PDF documents
* AI-generated content flows

Elements also connects with the broader Unlayer platform. Developers can define content structure in code, and when visual editing is needed, teams can bring that work into Unlayer’s Builder so marketers, admins, or end users can edit without touching code.

## **Our Ask**

We’re open sourcing this early because we want feedback from people building with React, Next.js, email, PDFs, templates, and AI-generated content.

We’d love for you to:

1. Try it and tell us what feels useful or missing.
2. Star the GitHub repo if you want to support the project.
3. Share examples of emails, pages, PDFs, invoices, reports, or AI-generated content workflows you’d want Elements to support.

GitHub: <https://github.com/unlayer/elements>\
Docs: <https://docs.unlayer.com/elements>

Would love feedback from the YC community.

Email: [founders@unlayer.com](mailto:founders@unlayer.com)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** [**Unlayer**](https://unlayer.com) is an AI-powered content creation platform for developers. It gives you **embeddable builders**, templates, APIs, and AI toolkit so your users can create **emails**, **pages**, **documents**, and other content directly **inside your product**.

<https://youtu.be/qp9t74G4VyM>

—

## The Problem

Almost every software product eventually needs users to create content.

Emails, landing pages, proposals, invoices, documents, announcements, templates, PDFs, and more.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102816&key=user_uploads/105300/df31db0c-923c-4ac3-977d-bd881f9586d1)

At first, this looks like “just add an editor.” Then you need responsive rendering, templates, merge tags, asset management, permissions, versioning, exports, personalization, localization, and now AI generation.

A small feature quietly becomes an entire content creation platform.

—

## What We Built

**Unlayer gives developers the building blocks to add AI-powered content creation into their own products.**

You can embed visual builders for emails, pages, popups, and documents, then connect them to templates, file storage, exports, APIs, and AI workflows.

Your users can visually create and edit content. Your AI agents can generate, personalize, translate, and modify that content through APIs and skills.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102816&key=user_uploads/105300/c9995728-e131-44cd-93cc-d295f255cf1b)

Over time, Unlayer has grown to **1,000+ customers**, from startups to teams at **Netflix**, **Fidelity**, **Bank of America**, **Mastercard, Twilio, Chargebee**, and others.

That has given us a front-row seat into the same pattern: almost every product eventually needs users or AI to create content inside the product itself.

—

## Why AI Changes This

Content creation is moving from manual editing to assisted and automated workflows.

A user should be able to say:

* **_“Create a launch email for this feature.”_**
* **_“Translate this landing page into Spanish.”_**
* **_“Turn this proposal into a branded PDF.”_**
* **_“Personalize this announcement for each customer segment.”_**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102816&key=user_uploads/105300/639a8626-7790-4094-b684-c4800407a6c6)

But for AI to do this well inside a product, it needs more than a text box. It needs access to templates, design structure, brand rules, assets, exports, and the final builder where humans can review and edit.

That is what we are building with Unlayer.

—

## Our Vision

We think the future of content creation inside software has two interfaces:

1. A visual builder for people
2. An action layer for AI agents

# TLDR:

We are excited to launch [Haven](https://haven.run/)’s fine-tuning platform for open source LLMs!

* Haven lets you fine-tune open source LLMs such as Llama or Mistral without writing code or setting up infrastructure. We charge $0.004/1k training tokens, and you get $5 in free credits after signing up
* You can host models for testing with <1s cold start times. We achieve this by running hundreds of model adapters on a single GPU and hot-swapping them based on user requests (will write more about this in a blog post)

You can get started [**here**](https://app.haven.run/) - alternatively, reach out to [**hello@haven.run**](https://app.haven.run/) or watch our [demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpyVKUyt7k8) if you want to learn more!

### **The Problem**

Over the last months, we’ve identified two big pain points that make it hard to work with open source models:

1. Open source models work best when they are trained for specific use cases, but the fine-tuning process with existing tools is super annoying. We have found that most of our time is spent setting up infrastructure to go from finishing a training run to actually testing our models, rather than actually writing code and improving our models
2. Hosting custom models is expensive. Running a single Llama-7B model in float16 requires at minimum an A10 GPU, which costs $700+ per month. To run ten or a hundred specialized models for common tasks, this would mean that we have a monthly AWS bill of $7,000 or $70,000, respectively.

### **The Solution**

Haven’s platform offers a super simple way to fine-tune models without managing infrastructure or writing code, and to test and run them with low costs and without any additional work.

We are able to provide a super short feedback loop of going from training to running a fine-tuned model by hosting multiple lora adapters in parallel. This makes it possible for us to host hundreds of fine-tuned models on-demand on a single GPU. For our users, this reduced model cold start times to <1s and internally, we are able to host a single fine-tuned model for a couple of dollars per month. We also enable our users to export their model weights to Huggingface, so that they can run models entirely on their terms.

### **Our Ask**

Feel free to check out our [**platform**](https://app.haven.run/) and give us feedback! After signing up, you’ll receive $5 in credits to train a couple of models :) We are also happy to answer questions at [**hello@haven.run**](https://app.haven.run/)

launches.title: renderlet: Making graphics programming easy
launches.tagline: Write graphics code that automatically runs anywhere
launches.body:
**Building interactive graphics is really hard**. Developers need expert-level knowledge of GPU programming just to build code that is not portable to new environments such as Web or Mobile or reusable across applications.

Renderlet is a WebAssembly framework for **writing graphics code that runs anywhere**. Describe your graphics pipeline using a **higher-level abstractions** and use renderlet to generate low-level, cross-platform rendering code.

With renderlet, developers can easily embed GPU-accelerated 2D and 3D graphics into cross-platform applications.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79415&key=user_uploads/1759368/4ce27e3c-1c68-456d-a0bd-eedd272c1712)

## How it works

With renderlet, **we compile graphics to portable WebAssembly modules** and provide a runtime that abstracts away the underlying GPU architecture to the code.

Developers can take advantage of modern technologies like **WebGPU** without having to learn the intricacies of yet another standard. 2D and 3D graphics are fully decoupled from the application and device and can ship decoupled from the applications code in a format that **runs anywhere**.

Renderlet is:

* A **compiler** that takes a high-level specification of your graphics pipeline - including custom assets, functions, and libraries - and builds self-contained WebAssembly rendering modules
* A  **renderer**, _wander_, that embeds into any application on any platform that and safely runs rendering modules with the GPU
* A **visual editor** that makes it easy to build entire graphics and visualization pipelines out of reusable rendering modules

**Anybody should be able to build interactive applications** without having to be a graphics programming expert.  

## About Us

[Sean Isom](https://linkedin.com/in/isom) previously built developer platforms at Adobe as a Lead Engineer and Sr. Engineering Manager. He helped bring products to the cloud and web using tools like WebAssembly and is currently involved in standardization efforts for WebAssembly GPU support.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79415&key=user_uploads/1759368/36bcf46c-edd6-4b90-9124-45c3c81ec64b)

## What’s next?

Our cross-platform rendering engine, **wander**, is open source: <https://github.com/renderlet/wander/> 

We’re kicking off with a **live demo** today of renderlet at Wasm I/O!  <https://2024.wasmio.tech/sessions/paint-by-numbers-high-performance-drawing-in-wasm/>

They were all built to abstract away code, but we’re in a new era of product development—where code isn’t the barrier. The real challenge is giving builders the best way to work with it. In other words, creating things with code has become more of a UX problem than a technical one.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=87467&key=user_uploads/137575/f4e651b1-8cc2-4f41-8512-09500cf2cd0d)

Our product can be best described as a visual IDE – you can either start with building a new app from a prompt, or import your existing NextJS / Tailwind app with Onlook. Once you run your app, you can start designing the interface directly as it’s rendered.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=87467&key=user_uploads/137575/7a85a948-73c8-418f-9420-155cdec6d2de)

Want to change a color? Want to move a div? Want to create a new page? You can do it yourself, or ask Onlook’s AI chat to do it for you. Because everything is one-to-one in code, you’re creating the real product with your edits, and you can always right-click to view your code in your preferred code editor.

And, when you’re ready to share your creation with the world, you can host your project through Onlook with just a click.

### **How we got here**

We started Onlook because we had experienced both sides of the design / engineering gap. Daniel has been a designer for over a decade, and Kiet was an engineer at ServiceNow and Amazon working directly with designers. 

Kiet reached out to Daniel on YC’s Cofounder matching platform after starting the company in January of 2024, and shortly after we decided to team up and work together. If you’re looking for a cofounder, we [wrote a bit](https://onlook.substack.com/p/how-to-find-a-cofounder) about that process that you may find useful on our company Substack. 

We [launched on Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40904862) and the project quickly earned over 1k GitHub stars. People were compelled by the idea of an open-source visual editor for code, and it felt like the timing was right. Since launching, we’ve continued to refine our editor to make it even better, and have since earned **6.8k stars**, tons of contributions.

Also, Onlook was recently ranked as the **#1 trending repo on GitHub**!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=87467&key=user_uploads/137575/79a6fb56-14c8-4c1e-b815-9261e651199a)

### **Use Onlook**

You can get started today by [downloading Onlook](http://onlook.com/download?utm_source=launch_yc&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=yc_launch). 

People use Onlook for **prototyping ideas**, for **building their product**, and for **hosting their website**. Thanks to [Paratus Health](https://paratushealth.com/), [SalesPatriot](https://salespatriot.com/), [Calltree.ai](http://Calltree.ai), [NextByte](https://trynextbyte.com/), [Casixty](https://casixty.com/), [TrainLoop](https://trainloop.ai/), and [Scout](https://www.scoutforschools.com/) for being early partners and for using Onlook to build their sites and products!

Feel free to [browse our open issues and contribute](https://github.com/onlook-dev/onlook/issues), or [support the project with a star](https://github.com/onlook-dev/onlook/)! ⭐  
* **Follow us** – We put out a lot of content in a lot of places:
  * Join our [Discord community](https://discord.gg/ZZzadNQtns)

Onlook is building **the uncompromising design and development tool** – One familiar to designers and infused with AI to make excellent code that developers love.

With Onlook, we hope to empower anyone to make incredible websites, incredibly fast, and we can’t wait to see what you create!

Cekura built an AI browser agent that can read how-to articles and navigate the product to verify if the articles are still valid. It saves documentation/customer success teams at SaaS companies hundreds of hours per week.

<https://youtu.be/JJR7hz3dPaQ>

The engineering team is releasing a new feature — hoorayyy! Guess who’s not excited — the documentation team. So many help articles are no longer up-to-date. They are now faced with 2 options:

1. Finding and reading through all the relevant product help articles (this will take literally 100+ hours of manual labor per week for some companies), or
2. Hoping that a dissatisfied customer will file a complaint instead of quietly churning.

launches.tagline: Hera reviews every drawing against your factory's own standards and the ASME code, catching expensive mistakes and preventing rework 10x faster than manual review.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Every custom metal part starts as a drawing, and every drawing gets checked by hand before anyone builds it. Hera does that check in minutes instead of a full day, and catches the mistakes that turn into scrapped parts.**

[**https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y**](https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y)

**The Problem**

Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.

Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.

We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

**Our Solution**

Hera is a brain for manufacturing. Any real advance in manufacturing has to be grounded in two things: the standards parts are held to and the reality of the shop floor. So that's what we built Hera on.

Upload a drawing and Hera checks GD&T callouts, tolerance stack ups, and title block requirements against ASME Y14.5, relevant ISO standards, and your own design intent. The result is a drawing your shop can build right the first time, without the delays and rework that eat margins. Every review also makes Hera more valuable, creating a system of record for drawing errors that helps teams build better models for engineering processes.

**While the current review takes days, Hera takes minutes… and gets better by the drawing.**

**Us**

**Noelle** grew up in an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines and has been on factory floors her whole life. At 19, she built a water-treatment facility that added 40 L/s of capacity to the park. 

**Meera** has spent years around manufacturing: at her family's plants, and on projects at Pfizer and TE Connectivity, where she built a SOTA discrete-event simulation. She taught herself PLC programming and C++, and has published ML research at UW.

We actually met on a bus to a factory tour, and have been best friends ever since!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107030&key=user_uploads/3352287/d05e9e1a-57c8-4e43-91d7-75e42a004261)

**Our Ask** If you run or work at a factory (aerospace, semiconductor, medical device, pressure vessel, or custom machinery), we want to visit you! If you invite us out to see your shop, we’ll come by in person and bring you a **customized Hera Swiss Army knife**.

Reach out to us at [**founders@manufacturingintelligence.org**](mailto:founders@manufacturingintelligence.org).
